title: A Multi-Center Dataset and Benchmark for SYNTAX Segmentation of Coronary Angiograms
abstract: arXiv:2607.22139v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Dense pixel-level classification of coronary angiography is essential for automated cardiovascular diagnostics, yet the computer vision community lacks gold-standard protocols and robust datasets to tackle this topologically complex, heavily long-tailed domain. To bridge this gap, we introduce CARDIAG: a rigorous, multi-center benchmark dataset designed to evaluate deep learning architectures on fine-grained SYNTAX segment classification. Unlike prior efforts, CARDIAG systematically prevents patient- and center-level data leakage while providing an unprecedented suite of annotations: highly imbalanced multi-class labels, explicit catheter and stenosis masks, expert uncertainty maps, temporal sequence frames, and spatial metadata. Using CARDIAG, we conduct the most extensive architectural sweep in this domain, benchmarking 24 models spanning classic CNNs, Vision Transformers (ViTs), and State-Space Models (SSMs). translated_title: 用于冠状动脉血管造影SYNTAX分割的多中心数据集与基准测试
translated_abstract: 冠状动脉血管造影的密集像素级分类对于自动化心血管诊断至关重要，然而计算机视觉界缺乏金标准协议和鲁棒的数据集来应对这一拓扑复杂、长尾分布严重的领域。为了弥合这一差距，我们推出了CARDIAG：一个严谨的多中心基准数据集，旨在评估深度学习架构在细粒度SYNTAX节段分类上的表现。与以往的研究不同，CARDIAG系统地防止了患者级和中心级的数据泄露，同时提供了前所未有的丰富注释套件：高度不平衡的多类别标签、显式的导管与狭窄掩膜、专家不确定性图、时序序列帧以及空间元数据。利用CARDIAG，我们开展了该领域最广泛的架构评估，对涵盖经典CNN、视觉Transformer（ViTs）和状态空间模型（SSMs）在内的24个模型进行了基准测试。
tldr: 该论文推出了CARDIAG——首个针对冠状动脉造影SYNTAX节段分割的多中心基准数据集，通过严格防止患者级和中心级数据泄露并提供前所未有的丰富注释（不平衡多类标签、导管与狭窄掩膜、专家不确定性图等），同时对24种涵盖CNN、ViT和SSM的深度学习架构进行了该领域最广泛的基准评估。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces CARDIAG, a rigorous multi-center benchmark dataset for SYNTAX segment segmentation of coronary angiograms, which systematically prevents patient- and center-level data leakage, provides an unprecedented suite of annotations (imbalanced multi-class labels, catheter and stenosis masks, expert uncertainty maps), and conducts the most extensive architectural benchmarking of 24 models spanning CNNs, ViTs, and SSMs.
